name: PIZZA HUT 12" Pepperoni Pizza, Hand-Tossed Crust (USDA food medium)
description: Food-derived medium from USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy): measured amino acids, sugars, fatty acids, vitamins and minerals of PIZZA HUT 12" Pepperoni Pizza, Hand-Tossed Crust, plus a mineral base. Measured nutrients with no curated BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered; non-metabolite aggregates (energy, protein, total fat/fibre) are excluded by design.

provenance.citation: U.S. Department of Agriculture, FoodData Central (SR Legacy), fdc.nal.usda.gov (FDC ID 173279).
provenance.notes: USDA measured nutrients mapped to BiGG via a curated nutrient->exchange table; amounts (per 100 g) in usda_amount/usda_unit. Unmapped measured metabolites kept in uncovered (v2). Aggregates excluded.
provenance.license_name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication
provenance.url_status_note: USDA FoodData Central returns HTTP 404 for food-details URLs while its single-page app renders the correct food page client-side (verified 2026-09-06: curl -> 404 with an identical app shell for every id; headless Chromium -> the correct title and nutrient table). The link works for a reader and fails for a link-checker. Do not retire it.

components.mapping_note: source name destroyed at build time; it was one of Cystine / Cysteine and the two collide on this exchange; build_usda_media_v2.py NMAP_RAW; [CHEM-CYS-01] USDA nutrient 1216 "Cystine" is L-cystine, the disulfide DIMER (C6H12N2O4S2, InChIKey LEVWYRKDKASIDU-IMJSIDKUSA-N, BiGG id cysi__L). It was mapped to cys__L, L-cysteine, the MONOMER (C3H7NO2S, XUJNEKJLAYXESH-REOHCLBHSA-N) -- a different skeleton and 2x stoichiometry -- and stamped "exact". The two USDA nutrients "Cystine" and "Cysteine" additionally collide on the same exchange key, so one measured amount silently overwrote the other. The source nutrient name was destroyed at build time (the record stores the BiGG name), so which of the two produced any given row is UNRECOVERABLE from the shipped data: the row cannot be retargeted, only relabelled and flagged. Correct target for future builds is cysi__L; see tools/curation/usda_nutrient_table.tsv.

components.mapping_note: source name destroyed at build time; it was one of MUFA 18:1 c / MUFA 18:1 and the two collide on this exchange; build_usda_media_v2.py NMAP_RAW; [CLASS-USDA-181] USDA reaches ocdcea only through the class strings "MUFA 18:1 c" and "MUFA 18:1", both of which name a chain-length:unsaturation CLASS covering every C18:1 positional and geometric isomer. components.mapping_note: build_usda_media_v2.py MINMAP; [CHEM-SE-01] USDA "Selenium, Se" is a TOTAL ELEMENTAL selenium assay. slnt is selenite, O3Se -- one specific oxyanion. Dietary selenium is predominantly selenomethionine and selenocysteine, not the selenite ion, and selenite has dedicated reductase and sulfur-assimilation routes in many GEMs. The element measurement cannot certify an oxidation state, so this is recorded as a declared species proxy, never as an exact identity. FLUX WARNING for the bounds workstream: 6,468 food media open EX_slnt_e at lower_bound -1000 on the strength of a total-Se number, and selenite is not otherwise supplied by the injected mineral base.

Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
